claims.text: Pulumi can reference existing Terraform state files.
Pulumi programs can use any Terraform provider.
Pulumi can import and use Terraform modules directly.
HCL code can be converted to Pulumi code.
Terraform and Pulumi deployments can be orchestrated together.
The `pulumi import` command can be used to bring Terraform-managed resources under Pulumi management.
Pulumi provides a `terraform.state.S3Reference` API/type for referencing Terraform state stored in an S3 bucket.
The `pulumi import` CLI command accepts a syntax of the form `pulumi import <type>:<subtype>:<Type> <name> <id>`, e.g. `pulumi import aws:ec2/vpc:Vpc main-vpc vpc-12345`.
Pulumi provides a `@pulumi/policy` package exporting `PolicyPack` and `validateResourceOfType` for defining policy packs.
Pulumi provides an Automation API accessible via `@pulumi/pulumi/automation`.
The Pulumi Automation API exposes a `LocalWorkspace.createOrSelectStack` method for creating or selecting a stack.
The Pulumi Automation API's stack object has an `up` method that accepts an `onOutput` callback option.
Pulumi provides a `pulumi.ComponentResource` base class for creating reusable component resources.
Pulumi component resources have a `registerOutputs` method used to register outputs.
There is a Pulumi documentation page at /docs/intro/concepts/ titled 'Pulumi Architecture & Concepts' covering Pulumi's architecture.
There is a Pulumi documentation page at /docs/using-pulumi/adopting-pulumi/ titled 'Adopting Pulumi' covering comprehensive migration strategies.

There is a Pulumi documentation page at /docs/insights/policy/ titled 'Policy as Code' covering infrastructure governance and compliance.

Issues about this guide can be opened at https://github.com/pulumi/docs/issues.
The Pulumi Automation API's stack `setConfig` method can set the `aws:region` configuration key, e.g. to the value "us-west-2".
An AWS S3 bucket resource in Pulumi has an `acl` property that can take values such as "public-read" or "public-read-write" to indicate public accessibility.
An AWS EC2 instance resource in Pulumi has a `tags` property.
